name: run.socially/socially
title: socially.run
description: Read public social profiles and posts, and search videos, news and trends.

tools.name: resolve_target
tools.description: Turn a profile URL, post URL, website or @handle into what socially would read: the platform, the kind (profile, post, website), the normalized handle and the one canonical URL. No egress, no credit. Use it to validate input before a metered lookup.

input.description: A profile URL, post URL, website or @handle.

platform.description: Required when `input` is a bare handle.

tools.name: list_platforms
tools.description: List supported capabilities separately from source health. `capabilities` reports profile/post lookup, topic video search, indexed topic search, hashtag search and country trend boards. YouTube and TikTok support topic video search; only YouTube has a country board. Only Instagram has indexed topic search, the reels on its public popular page for a word, which exists for some words only. TikTok and Instagram support hashtag search. Google Trends is a separate `/trending` source. `status` and `strategies` describe profile reads; `postStatus` and `postStrategies` describe post reads, with verification dates and the last 24 hours of results. A supported capability can still have no working source here. Free.

tools.name: lookup_profile
tools.description: Read a public profile on Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, Facebook, GitHub or a website. A `found` answer includes the profile, recent posts and platform details when available: account ids, links, creation dates and public counts. Instagram's `userId` and `graphId` name different ids; neither grants permission. Missing fields are null; unsupported blocks are absent. Data outcomes answer 200: `found`, `notFound` (confirmed by the platform, cached an hour) or `undecided` (refunded, never cached). 1 credit on a miss, 0 on a hit. `extractedAt` is the original read time, including cache and snapshot hits.

input.description: A profile URL, post URL, website or @handle.

platform.description: Required when `input` is a bare handle.

posts.description: Recent posts to return (0–15). Default 10. This limits the answer, not the source read.

refresh.description: Bypass the cache and the snapshot; costs a credit even when fresh.

tools.name: lookup_post
tools.description: Read one public Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn or Facebook post or GitHub repository by URL. Returns its caption, author id, date, media and public counts when available. X, LinkedIn and Facebook posts are read only through a paid reader, with exact counts, and a deployment with no reader configured answers 503 before it charges. A LinkedIn post's `author.profileUrl` is the person's or the company's own page, and a Facebook post's `likes` counts every reaction. A full Instagram read adds source ids and ordered `frames` with image/video URLs, dimensions, duration and alt text; missing fields are null. YouTube adds video/channel ids, title and description, not a playable stream. GitHub adds repository details (language, license, default branch, topics, stars, forks, open issues and watchers). Every read says its `detailLevel` (`detailed` from the post's own page or API, `embed` from a thin public card that leaves what it does not show null) and its `confidence`; a cached answer keeps both. CDN URLs can expire: download the files. Answers `found` or `undecided` (refunded), never `notFound`. 1 credit on a miss, 0 on a hit. Cached answers keep the original `extractedAt`.

refresh.description: Bypass the cache and the snapshot; costs a credit even when fresh.

tools.name: read_website
tools.description: Fetch a public page through the proxy and return its readable text, title, description, images and ld+json. Pages that render with JavaScript are rendered when the budget allows (`render: auto`). Private and internal addresses answer 400 SSRF_BLOCKED. 1 credit on a miss, 0 on a hit (24 h).

maxChars.description: Cap on the readable text. Default 8,000.

render.description: `always` renders every time and never falls back to a plain fetch. It spends render budget and fails closed at RENDER_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED; a deployment with no renderer answers SIDECAR_UNAVAILABLE.

refresh.description: Bypass the cache and the snapshot; costs a credit even when fresh.

tools.name: fetch_og
tools.description: The Open Graph card a page publishes: title, description, image, site name, type, locale, canonical URL. 1 credit on a miss, 0 on a hit (24 h).

refresh.description: Bypass the cache and the snapshot; costs a credit even when fresh.

tools.name: list_trending
tools.description: One country's board: Google's rising searches, each with the news behind it and an approximate volume, or YouTube's most popular videos. A board stays fresh in the cache for ten minutes. A cached board costs 0 credits. When the source refuses us, the last good board is served instead, flagged `stale` with the time it was captured, and it costs nothing either: you are charged for a reading, never for an attempt.

source.description: Which board to read: `google` for what a country is searching, `youtube` for what it is watching.

geo.description: The country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (US, BR, ES). REQUIRED: a board is one country's board, and there is no honest default for whose. This used to fall back to `US`, which meant a caller in São Paulo was quietly handed the American one. A country the source does not publish answers 400 and says so. For a subject rather than a country, see `search_news` and `search_youtube`. A trending board takes no query.

category.description: YouTube's video category id: `10` is Music, `17` Sport. YouTube only: Google Trends publishes no categories.

limit.description: Entries to return, 1–50. Google publishes ten per country.

tools.name: search_youtube
tools.description: What creators are publishing about a subject, in the order YouTube ranks it: title, channel, exact view count, duration and the description snippet, plus real upload dates, likes and comments when the deployment holds a Data API key (`stats: "exact"`). Read from the results page rather than the API's 100-unit search, so one key's day holds thousands of these. The answer is cached for thirty minutes, and the same question again costs nothing.

q.description: What to search for, the way you would type it into YouTube.

limit.description: Videos to return, 1–20. One page is one read: a larger `limit` on the same question is served from it.

recency.description: Only videos uploaded within the window: `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Absent means any time.

sort.description: `relevance` uses YouTube's ranking. `views` puts the most-watched videos first. Combine `views` with `recency` to find popular uploads within that window, not to measure growing views. Without a window, `views` includes all-time hits.

country.description: The country to rank for, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (BR, US, ES). Omit it for YouTube's own ranking rather than a country's.

language.description: The language to ask and read the page in, ISO 639-1 (en, pt, es). Omit it and your `accept-language` header decides.

refresh.description: Read the page again instead of serving the half-hour cache. Charged like any read, and the fresh answer replaces the cached one.

tools.name: search_news
tools.description: What the press published about a subject inside a window: headline, publisher, and the date the story ran, read from Google News' public search feed. This is the subject half of trending: a trending board takes no query at all, so `q` plus `recency` is how you ask what is being said about one thing right now. Links are Google's own redirect, not the publisher's URL. Cached for ten minutes.

q.description: The subject to read about, the way you would say it.

limit.description: Stories to return, 1–50. One feed is one read: a larger `limit` on the same question is served from it.

recency.description: Only stories published within the window: `day`, `week`, `month` or `year`. Absent means any time, which for news is rarely the question.

country.description: The Google News edition, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (BR, US, ES). There is no worldwide edition: leave it out and one is chosen from `language`. The answer always says which one ran.

language.description: The edition's language, ISO 639-1 (en, pt, es). Default `en`.

refresh.description: Read the feed again instead of serving the ten-minute cache. Charged like any read.

tools.name: search_instagram
tools.description: The reels Instagram lists on its public popular page for a topic: shortcode, author, caption, exact play count and the date read off the media id. This is indexed discovery, not a hashtag feed. Instagram publishes these pages for some words only (`art`, `travel` and `music` have one; `fitness` and `nasa` did not when measured), lists up to 12 reels, and says in `hasMore` when it has more that cannot be read without signing in. A word with no page answers `indexed: false` and costs nothing. Cached for thirty minutes.

q.description: The topic, the way Instagram names its popular pages: one word or a few ("travel", "street photography"). Not every word has a page.

limit.description: Reels to return, 1–12. One page is one read: a smaller `limit` on the same topic is served from it.

refresh.description: Read the page again instead of serving the half-hour cache. Charged like any read, and the fresh answer replaces the cached one.

tools.name: search_github
tools.description: Three GitHub discovery reads in one call: `mode: repositories` (default) searches public repositories by keyword, language, push window and stars/forks; `mode: users` searches developers and organizations by keyword, location, language and followers/repositories, returning each account's bio, company, location, website, X handle and exact counts; `mode: trending` reads GitHub's trending repositories page (`daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`, optionally by language) with stars gained in the window. Cached for thirty minutes.

mode.description: `repositories` (default) searches public repositories, `users` searches developers and organizations for lead discovery, and `trending` reads GitHub's trending repositories board (`github.com/trending`).

q.description: What to search for (`repositories` and `users` modes). Omit on `trending` mode, or when filtering by `language` or `location` alone.

language.description: Programming language filter, such as `typescript`, `python` or `rust`.

location.description: Location filter for `users` mode, such as `Brazil` or `São Paulo`.

accountType.description: Filter `users` mode to personal accounts (`user`) or organizations (`org`).

recency.description: Window filter: `day`, `week`, `month` or `year` on `repositories` (by last push), or `day`, `week` or `month` on `trending` (`daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`).

limit.description: Items to return, 1–30. One page is one read: a smaller `limit` on the same question is served from it.

refresh.description: Read again instead of serving the half-hour cache. Charged like any read, and the fresh answer replaces the cached one.

tools.name: get_attributions
tools.description: Every upstream project whose data socially vendors or whose tool it runs, with its licence and the credit line to display. No API key needed. These credits are a licence obligation, not a feature.
